event.tilda_heart2.0.text: Oh, [player]! Just the account I wanted. Come here. This one won't fit in a bag.
event.tilda_heart2.0.why: sets up the hand-taught recipe: the one thing the shop cannot bag

event.tilda_heart2.2.text: She wrote down one recipe in her whole life. It's somewhere behind the flour sacks. I've never once moved the flour.
event.tilda_heart2.2.why: plants the exact spot heart 8 pays off, and why the flour never moves

event.tilda_heart4.intro.text: Come around the counter. Nobody comes back here but me. Mind Ledger. It's auditing.
event.tilda_heart4.intro.why: names the shipped window cat; auditing fits the slate reveal

dlg.tilda.slate.1.text: I ruled you a column the day you arrived. It's been waiting. What do I write under your name?
dlg.tilda.slate.1.why: the blank space was deliberate: she planned on the player staying

dlg.tilda.hours.1.text: Wetherell isn't shrinking, I tell myself. Then a whole morning brings two customers, and I can name them both. What do you think?
dlg.tilda.hours.1.why: naming both customers is smaller and sadder than a bell count; also stops two lines opening on 'I'

dlg.tilda.hours.r2.text: Gently. Recounting with kindness. I'll try it. Ledger can check my sums.
dlg.tilda.hours.r2.why: cat name consistency with the shipped window line

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.2.text: Go on, judge. One scarecrow gets the field. The other guards my rhubarb.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.2.why: stakes instead of a bare question; funniest word last

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r2.text: A tie. That word costs extra in here. Take one anyway, and we'll both be wounded together.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r2.why: 'Coward' teased the player; now the tease lands on the word, not them

dlg.tilda.birthday.r1.text: A flower, in my shop! It goes in the window, beside the good parsnips.
dlg.tilda.birthday.r1.why: her birthday is Spring 12; a pumpkin in the window was out of season

dlg.tilda.birthday.r2.text: You'd mind it? That's the best present. Take the stool. Ledger bites coins, not customers.

event.tilda_friend.ask.text: Saturday stocktake, and the window needs three sunflowers. I sold mine. Excellent business, terrible planning.
event.tilda_friend.ask.why: shopkeeper arithmetic: her own stock betrayed her

event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l1.text: Wren. Your new chalkboard. Lovely frame. Remarkably familiar idea.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l1.why: slyer opener; lets Wren's flattery comeback land harder

event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l1.text: I've heard something about a cat, a windowsill, and Marcus's lunch.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l1.why: a third ingredient makes the gossip tradable; food gossip stays affectionate

event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l4.text: To old friends, dear. The crust is mine. The fish goes to Ledger.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l4.why: cat name consistency; she still will not eat fish

adds.text: I've chalked it already. 'One cauliflower, someday.' The slate takes vague debts, but it takes them seriously.
adds.why: the bible says heart 2 introduces the slate; a debt means the player comes back

threads.tilda_heart2: Her mother wrote down exactly one recipe, it is somewhere behind the flour, and Tilda has never moved the flour.
threads.tilda_heart5: There is a chair with the player's shape in it on Thursday, and she will not really bake fewer scones.
threads.story_notes_tilda: Two more doors get notes before closing, and the player is left wondering whose, and whether they ever got one.
threads.story_scarecrows: Rematch next fall, and the runner-up scarecrow now stands in the player's field holding a grudge.
threads.tilda_heart4: The player's name is on the slate now, which by Tilda's arithmetic means they have to come back.
threads.tilda_heart6: A whole morning can bring two customers she can name, and Felix must never hear about it.
threads.tilda_heart8: The pumpkin pie card is out of the tin at last; Saturday, the tin, or the whole village decides what it becomes.
threads.tilda_heart10: The farm is on the sign in paint, not chalk, and the player wonders what a supplier owes a shop that believed first.
threads.tilda_friend: The window is saved and the slate has a new entry nobody asked her to write.
threads.tilda_birthday: Something now sits at the top of the slate where she will read it first thing every morning.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_2: 'Thin Ice' is still on the slate in capitals, and Felix still walks straight past it.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_3: Tea for two again: the player wonders how many years she has been making the second cup.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_4: The crust-for-fish treaty stands, and Ledger eats better than either of them.
threads.overheard_tilda_juno_1: A smiley-face hinge is priceless, so somewhere in the shop there must be a shelf of things she cannot charge for.
threads.overheard_tilda_juno_3: Juno's forge will open next door to Bram, probably, okay, definitely, and Tilda has promised the first shelf.

notes: Fixed dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r2: 'Coward.' was aimed at the player, which my voice rules forbid; the tease now lands on the word 'tie' instead.

tilda_heart10: my bible says I hand over the original two-note shop bell at heart 10, but the scene only gives pumpkin pie and plays sfx coin. If mechanics ever reopen, swap the sfx to bell and consider a bell beat; I did not touch items this round.
dlg.tilda.birthday.r1 said the flower goes 'beside the good pumpkin'; my birthday is Spring 12, so no pumpkin is in season. Now it sits beside the parsnips, which also calls back the planting line.
I renamed 'the cat' to Ledger in four lines to match the shipped window-cat line; the heart 4 intro, heart 6 recount, birthday stool and fish-pie toast now all agree on who runs audits.
